report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/gui/lint.py; verified docstring claims against code, identified a few discrepancies.
risks: analyse() | medium | metric values may be negative or unrealistic if capture keys missing; no validation | inspect a real capture
compare() | medium | assumes all reports share identical metric keys; heterogeneous reports will KeyError | test with mismatched reports
main() | low | writes report.json to runs/gui relative to CWD; may overwrite existing | check CWD expectations

handoff.purpose: Compute objective and proxy metrics over a DOM/CSSOM capture; compare reports and write evidence.

symbols.name: BANNED_FACES
symbols.note: Tuple of font-family names treated as generated defaults.

symbols.name: _looks_like_identifier
symbols.note: Heuristic: single-word lowercase strings with underscores, or raw JSON-like text.

symbols.name: _lum
symbols.note: Relative luminance per WCAG, using sRGB linearization.

symbols.name: contrast_ratio
symbols.note: WCAG contrast ratio between two RGB tuples.

symbols.name: Metric
symbols.note: Dataclass holding a measurement and its evidence; to_dict truncates offenders to 12.

symbols.name: _sel
symbols.note: Builds a short selector string from element dict.

symbols.name: _is_panel
symbols.note: True if element has borderSides >=1 and size >=56x24.

symbols.name: _contains
symbols.note: Geometric containment with strict area ordering.

symbols.name: analyse
symbols.note: Computes all metrics from a capture dict; returns report dict.

symbols.name: compare
symbols.note: Builds a side-by-side text table of metric values across reports.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry: reads capture JSON files, writes runs/gui/report.json, prints comparison.

claims.text: Reads a capture from probe.js and computes metrics over the DOM/CSSOM.
claims.why: analyse() takes a capture dict and computes metrics from element geometry and computed style fields.

claims.text: No pixels are inspected; every number here is derived from geometry and computed style
claims.why: All metrics use fields like w, h, x, y, fontSize, fontWeight, fg, bgEff, radiusPx, etc.; no image data is referenced.

claims.text: Tier A metrics (contrast, overflow, target size, banned faces) measure things that are true or false. They can gate.
claims.why: Those four metrics are tagged tier 'A' and are counts of objective conditions.

claims.text: Tier B metrics are PROXIES ... Each proxy carries its own agreement record ... a proxy that stops tracking the human verdict gets retired rather than defended.
claims.why: The chunk does not include any agreement record or retirement mechanism; only metric objects with note fields.

claims.text: every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it
claims.why: Each Metric includes an offenders list; even when empty, the list is present.

claims.text: Thresholds are stamped ASSUMED until the corpus is large enough to earn MEASURED. Right now the corpus is n=4 (three rejected surfaces, one approved)
claims.why: No threshold stamping or corpus size is present in this chunk.

claims.text: stdlib only, by design
claims.why: Imports are json, math, collections.Counter, dataclasses, pathlib; no third-party imports.

claims.text: A framed surface, not a hairline divider or a text run.
claims.why: Requires borderSides >=1 and size >=56x24, which excludes hairlines and text runs.

claims.text: WCAG AA: 4.5:1 body, 3.0:1 large
claims.why: need is 4.5 unless large (fontSize >=18 or >=14 bold), then 3.0.

claims.text: interactive targets should reach 44x44
claims.why: Flags elements with w<44 or h<44.

claims.text: grotesk defaults that mark a generated page
claims.why: Checks first font family against BANNED_FACES.

claims.text: a broken page is not a design question
claims.why: Counts consoleErrors from capture.

claims.text: raw density of what is on screen at once
claims.why: Uses cap['elementsKept'] as count.

claims.text: when everything is a bordered box, nothing is elevated
claims.why: Counts panels identified by _is_panel.

claims.text: more than two or three corner radii reads as unconsidered
claims.why: Counts distinct rounded radius values among panels.

claims.text: frames inside frames inside frames
claims.why: Computes deepest geometric nesting chain.

claims.text: shouted micro-labels used as decoration rather than hierarchy
claims.why: Measures share of uppercase-transformed or all-caps text.

claims.text: if everything is flagged, nothing is flagged
claims.why: Counts small pill-like elements with borders or background.

claims.text: an N-equal-tile metric row is the most recognisable trope in the category
claims.why: Finds largest group of same-size elements in a row band.

claims.text: distinct 30-degree hue families in use, semantic colour included
claims.why: Buckets hues by //30 and counts families with >=2 occurrences.

claims.text: internal field names and raw JSON rendered as user-facing text
claims.why: Uses _looks_like_identifier to flag such strings.

claims.text: Side-by-side table. The point of the whole exercise: do the numbers separate the surfaces a human rejected from the one he approved?
claims.why: Prints a table with optional human verdicts row.

observations.what: Metric values are not clamped; e.g. allcaps_text_share can exceed 100% if caps_len > total_text, and contrast_ratio can be infinite if lo=0.
compare() assumes all reports have identical metric keys and same order; if not, next() raises StopIteration.
main() writes to 'runs/gui/report.json' relative to CWD, not necessarily the module directory; may overwrite an existing report.

_looks_like_identifier rejects strings with spaces, so multi-word identifiers or JSON with spaces are not flagged; the docstring says 'raw JSON on the glass' but only checks for leading '{"' or '{ "'.
The 'visible_elements' metric uses cap['elementsKept'] without checking existence, unlike other cap.get() calls; a capture missing that key raises KeyError.
